candidates.title: Effect of Obicetrapib on Glycaemia and New-Onset Diabetes: Pooled Analysis of BROADWAY/BROOKLYN and an Updated Meta-analysis of CETP Inhibitor Trials.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: New-onset diabetes (NoD) is a recognised effect of statin therapy potentially influencing acceptance of intensive LDL-C-lowering. In contrast, cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) inhibition has been associated with lower NoD risk in earlier trials. We assessed the effect of the highly selective CETP inhibitor obicetrapib on glycaemia and NoD, contextualised within an updated meta-analysis of CETP inhibitor trials.
METHODS: Individual participant data from the phase 3 BROADWAY and BROOKLYN trials were pooled across 1,700 participants without diabetes at baseline (899 normoglycaemic, 801 prediabetes; 38.8% women), randomised 2:1 to obicetrapib 10 mg or placebo for 52 weeks. The PRISMA-compliant, PROSPERO-registered systematic review identified six eligible trials reporting NoD. Pooled risk ratios were calculated using Mantel-Haenszel fixed-effect models, with prespecified subgroup analyses by baseline glycaemic status and CETPi potency, and trial-level meta-regression.
RESULTS: Obicetrapib did not increase HbA1c at week 52 vs placebo (LSMD -0.02%, 95% CI -0.04 to 0.00). NoD occurred in 6.4% (obicetrapib) versus 8.5% (placebo) (adjusted OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.47-1.03), directionally consistent across glycaemic strata. Restricted cubic spline analyses identified associations between HDL-C, apoA1 and Lp(a) changes and NoD risk, but not HbA1c change. In the meta-analysis, CETP inhibition was associated with a 16% lower risk of NoD (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.79-0.90; I2 = 0%).
CONCLUSIONS: Obicetrapib did not adversely affect glycaemia and was associated with a numerically lower risk of NoD, consistent with a CETP inhibitor class signal of a modestly lower risk. The PREVAIL trial will provide larger-longer evidence about obicetrapib and NoD.

candidates.title: Procedural Success, Predictors of Failure, and Clinical Outcomes of Conduction System Pacing in Korea: The Korean Conduction System Pacing (K-CSP) Registry.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP), particularly left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), is a promising physiologic pacing strategy, but large-scale Asian data are lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, predictors of failure, and clinical outcomes of CSP in a nationwide Korean multicenter registry.
METHODS: This observational registry included 2,215 consecutive patients undergoing attempted CSP at 35 Korean centers between January 2021 and June 2025. Capture types were classified using EHRA criteria.
RESULTS: Stylet-driven leads were used in 87.0%. CSP succeeded in 87.4% (1,932/2,211). Among 1,922 LBBAP patients, left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) was achieved in 35.1%, left fascicular pacing (LFP) in 31.3%, and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) in 17.2%. Independent predictors of CSP failure included prior open-heart surgery involving septal manipulation, right-sided approach, and male sex. Pacing parameters were stable over 17.0±10.8 months. CSP failure was associated with worse composite outcomes on unadjusted analysis, but these associations were attenuated and no longer significant after adjustment. Among LBBAP patients, LVSP was associated with a higher adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization (adjusted HR 3.04, 95% CI 1.05-8.73, p=0.039) than LBBP+LFP; however, this association was based on few events with wide confidence intervals and was not significant on unadjusted analysis.
CONCLUSION: In this large-scale Asian CSP registry, LBBAP was feasible and safe, performed predominantly with stylet-driven leads. Direct conduction system capture (LBBP+LFP) was associated with a lower adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization than LVSP, although this was based on few events; these findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in randomized trials.

candidates.title: Leadless Atrial Pacing Targeting Bachmann Bundle for Atrial Resynchronization: A Single Center Registry.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interatrial conduction delay (IACD) resulting from fibrosis or functional block in Bachmann bundle (BB) occurs often in patients with sinus node dysfunction (SND) and increases the risk of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pacing the BB in patients with SND may reduce AF burden. Little is known of the feasibility and effectiveness of BB leadless atrial pacemaker (BBLAP) implantation.
OBJECTIVE: To determine if BBLAP is safe, feasible and improves IACD.
METHODS: This registry prospectively enrolled 21 consecutive adults with baseline P wave duration (PWD) >120ms undergoing BBLAP for SND. Fluoroscopy, intracardiac echocardiography and left atrial conduction time (LACT) measurements from a decapolar coronary sinus (CS) catheter were used to facilitate implantation. BBLAP implant success was defined as improved PWD, P wave morphology, and LACT. Baseline and BBLAP LACT and PWD, axis, and morphology were compared.
RESULTS: Of the 21 patients enrolled, 17 had successful BBLAP (81%). Among those with successful BBLAP, baseline PWD was 150 (±21) ms, BBLAP PWD was 113 (±23) ms, a reduction of 37 (±13) ms, p < 0.001. BBLAP P wave axis was inferiorly directed in all cases. 8/8 patients with a negative terminal P wave in the inferior leads at baseline had correction with BBLAP. LACT decreased from 113 (±35) ms to 78 (±33) ms, mean difference 35 (±15) ms, p <0.001, with BBLAP. 13/17 patients demonstrated a shift in CS activation from proximal-distal activation to mid- or distal-proximal activation during BBLAP. In all cases there were no complications.
CONCLUSION: The BBLAP implant technique presented in this registry is feasible and reduced IACD. Further study on the effect of BBLAP on AF burden is needed.

candidates.title: Distal-to-Proximal Conduction System Ablation as a Bailout Strategy in Refractory Multi-Exit Purkinje-Related Premature Ventricular Contractions and Ventricular Fibrillation.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ablation of premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) originating from the Purkinje network-particularly those with multiple exit sites and morphologies-poses a significant clinical challenge. In refractory cases where conventional ablation fails, proximal conduction system ablation may represent a viable alternative strategy.
OBJECTIVE: to evaluate the safety and efficacy of proximal conduction system ablation in patients with refractory multi-exit Purkinje PVCs with diverse morphologies.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included consecutive patients with drug-refractory, symptomatic Purkinje PVCs who underwent proximal conduction system ablation. Multiple exit sites and morphologies were observed during mapping and ablation, indicating complex activation within the Purkinje network.
RESULTS: Among the 22 patients included, 14 (63.6%) had PVC-triggered ventricular fibrillation. Acute elimination of the PVC by distal-to-proximal conduction system ablation achieved in 21 patients (95.5%), while one procedure (4.5%) was discontinued at the patient's request due to the anticipated risk of conduction system injury. The initial site of earliest activation arose from the posterior fascicle in 63.6% (n=14), the septal fascicle in 22.7% (n=5) and the anterior fascicle in 13.6% (n=3). During ablation, all patients demonstrated a shift in the site of earliest activation. Conduction disturbances occurred in 5 patients (22.7%). During a median follow-up of 32.3 months (IQR 17.5-54.5), one patient (4.5%) experienced PVC recurrence requiring repeat ablation; however, no patient experienced recurrent ventricular fibrillation.
CONCLUSION: Distal-to-proximal conduction system ablation can be an effective bailout strategy for patients with refractory multi-exit fascicular/Purkinje-related PVCs and recurrent VF. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm its long-term safety and efficacy.

candidates.title: Distal Reinterventions after Branched Stented Anastomosis Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair (B-SAFER): A Report from a Prospective Trial.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Optimal timing for distal reintervention after frozen elephant trunk repair remains debated. We evaluated patient characteristics, clinical outcomes, and predictors of distal aortic reintervention following Branched Stented Anastomosis Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair (B-SAFER).
METHODS: From May 2021 to January 2025, 405 patients underwent B-SAFER in a prospective, single-arm, nonrandomized PS-IDE cohort. Among them, 117 patients required 148 distal reinterventions. Indications for initial repair were acute type A dissection (36/189, 31%), chronic dissection (62/138, 53%), and degenerative aneurysm (19/78, 16%). Most reinterventions (n=132, 92%) were planned. Primary endpoints were operative mortality, stroke, and paralysis. Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed survival and freedom from reintervention. Median follow-up was 1.3 years, and median time to reintervention was 8.7 months.
RESULTS: Mortality after first reintervention was 6.5% (n=8). Permanent stroke occurred in one patient (0.8%), with no cases of paralysis. Causes of death included sepsis (n=4), hemorrhagic shock (n=2), pulmonary embolism (n=1), and intracranial hemorrhage (n=1). Freedom from reintervention at 2 years was 64%, lowest in chronic dissections (48%), intermediate in degenerative aneurysms (71%), and highest in acute dissections (74%). Larger descending and abdominal aortic diameters were the strongest predictors of reintervention. Survival at 2.5 years was similar across groups (81% acute, 81% chronic, 77% degenerative).
CONCLUSIONS: Distal reinterventions after B-SAFER are common, safe, and are associated with acceptable early outcomes. Disease chronicity and aortic diameter predict reintervention risk. Frozen elephant trunk is an effective platform for staged aortic repair, and earlier reintervention in high-risk patients warrants further study. (245).

candidates.title: Pregnancy Outcomes After Living Kidney Donation.
candidates.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: People who become pregnant after living kidney donation may be at increased risk of pregnancy-related adverse outcomes, although the evidence is unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether pregnancies after living kidney donation are associated with a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes than matched pregnancies among nondonors.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This matched cohort study used provincial administrative health care databases from Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta, Canada, and included living female kidney donors aged 18 to 42 years who donated a kidney between July 1992 and August 2021 and subsequently had singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation. These pregnancies were matched 1:4 with singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation among female nondonors. Pregnancies in donors and nondonors were matched on delivery date, age at delivery, years between cohort entry and delivery, number of prior pregnancies, and income. Final follow-up occurred until March 2023. Outcome analysis occurred from August 2024 to September 2026.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia. Secondary outcomes included 12 maternal, fetal and neonatal adverse outcomes, including the individual components of the primary outcome, the composite of low birth weight or preterm birth, and small for gestational age at birth.
RESULTS: The sample included 385 pregnancies in 252 living kidney donors (mean [SD] age, 27.8 [5.0] years) matched to 1540 pregnancies in 1535 nondonors (mean [SD] age, 27.0 [4.8] years). The primary composite outcome of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia occurred in 46 donor pregnancies (11.9%) and 128 nondonor pregnancies (8.3%; risk ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.10-2.08). Among the 12 secondary outcomes, the 95% CI for the risk ratio excluded 1.00 for the outcome of small for gestational age, which occurred in 53 donor pregnancies (13.8%) and 121 nondonor pregnancies (7.9%) (risk ratio, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.37-2.52).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, pregnancy after living kidney donation was associated with a higher risk of the composite outcome of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia, when compared with matched pregnancies in nondonors. Most postdonation pregnancies were uncomplicated. These findings support counseling donor candidates who may become pregnant about this risk and informing the prenatal care of donors who become pregnant.

candidates.title: Pulmonary Vein Isolation With Contact-Force-Sensing Large-Tip Focal Pulsed Field Ablation Catheter With 3D Mapping for Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: Omny-IRE 12-month Results.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omny-IRE (NCT05971693) evaluated safety and effectiveness of a large-tip focal, multielectrode, contact-force-sensing, pulsed field ablation, basket catheter with electroanatomic mapping integration.
OBJECTIVE: Report 12-month (M) study outcomes.
METHODS: Pulmonary vein isolation was performed using the OMNYPULSE platform. Patients underwent follow-up through 12M postablation visit with electrocardiography (preprocedure, predischarge, and at 1, 3, 6, and 12M), 24-hour Holter monitoring (3, 6, and 12M), and remote rhythm monitoring (weekly: 1-5M; monthly: 6-12M; and symptom-triggered recordings). The secondary effectiveness endpoint was 12M freedom from documented symptomatic/asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia (≥30 s) and acute procedural failure. Device/procedure-related serious adverse events (SAEs), quality-of-life assessed by Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life (AFEQT) scores, and healthcare-utilization (cardiovascular-hospitalizations and antiarrhythmic drug [AAD] use) were also evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 188 enrolled patients, 136 comprised the main-phase-cohort for safety and effectiveness evaluations. In this cohort, 12M freedom from symptomatic/asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia was 82.5% (90.1% using standard-of-care monitoring only). Clinical success, defined as freedom from documented symptomatic arrhythmia and acute procedural failure, was 89.9%, while single procedural success was 89.2%. Device/procedure-related SAEs occurred in 2.9% of main-phase patients. Mean overall AFEQT score improved by 25.5 points from baseline to 12M. Cardiovascular-hospitalizations decreased by 40.9% versus the 12M preprocedure period, and Class I/III AAD use decreased by 49.3% 6-12M postablation versus baseline.
CONCLUSIONS: Omny-IRE results demonstrated the effectiveness, safety, and healthcare benefits of PFA with the OMNYPULSE platform.

candidates.title: CATHETER ABLATION VERSUS SHAM FOR SYMPTOMATIC ATRIAL FIBRILLATION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND BAYESIAN META-ANALYSIS OF RANDOMIZED TRIALS.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation reduces atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence and improves symptoms and quality of life (QoL), but sham-controlled trials have reported discordant results.
OBJECTIVE: To synthesise sham-controlled trials of AF ablation and identify why QoL results differ.
METHODS: We searched databases and registries for randomized trials of catheter ablation versus sham in symptomatic AF. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life (AFEQT) score, pooled using a Bayesian random-effects model. Certainty was rated with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation.
RESULTS: Four trials (468 patients) were eligible; three (448 patients) were pooled. Ablation improved AFEQT relative to sham by 13.5 points (95% credible interval [CrI] 1.6 to 26.9), with a posterior probability of benefit 0.98, of exceeding the 5-point minimal clinically important difference 0.94, and by 12.9 points (-0.4 to 27.1; probability 0.97 and 0.91) with PVI-SHAM-AF's primary estimator. Heterogeneity (τ 8.2 points, I2 85.3%) was largely attributed to PVI-SHAM-AF, which differed from the other trials in symptom severity, rhythm monitoring and assessment of blinding; without it, the difference was 18.9 points (6.7 to 31.4). Ablation reduced AF recurrence in every trial (pooled risk ratio 0.49, CrI 0.17-0.89). Certainty was moderate for AF burden and recurrence and low for QoL.
CONCLUSION: Compared with sham embedded in active rhythm control, catheter ablation reduces AF recurrence and burden and has a high probability of clinically important QoL benefit, although its magnitude remains uncertain. Trials differ in population, monitoring, and estimator, not direction of effect.

candidates.title: Non-Invasive Stimulation of the Median Nerve: Neuromodulation to Reduce Atrial Arrhythmias in Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (The Randomized BEAT-AF Pilot Study).
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-invasive low-level electrical stimulation of the median nerve favorably affects atrial electrophysiology and reduces inflammation.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether a novel wearable home-care neuromodulation device that performs median nerve stimulation (MNS) reduces atrial arrhythmias (AA) and related symptoms.
METHODS: BEAT-AF was a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled, 12-week pilot study. Patients with a paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) burden of 0.5-25% on ambulatory 14-day ECG (aECG) monitoring were randomized 1:1 to either MNS or Sham, using a wristband-like neuromodulation and ECG monitoring device.
RESULTS: Among 31 patients (n=15 MNS / n=16 Sham; age 67.3±9.7; 23 M / 8 F; CHA2DS2-VASc 2.6±1.7; median AF burden 4.9% [IQR 5.2%]),immediate pre-/post-treatment ECG recordings demonstrated a 35% reduction in premature atrial contraction (PAC) burden with MNS versus a 7% increase with Sham (p=0.039).Comparing baseline to 12-week 14-day ECGs, PAC burden was reduced by 26.5% (p=0.046) vs a numerical change of +3.94% (p=0.94; Sham, between group p=0.46), and the adjusted median AF burden numerically was reduced by 63% (MNS) vs 4.1% (Sham; p=0.42). By EHRA classification, symptomatology improved with MNS (0.45 vs 0.02 reduction in score; p=0.017), with a 26.3% shift from EHRA Class III to I with MNS) (vs Sham; p=0.048).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with paroxysmal AF, non-invasive median nerve stimulation reduced PAC burden and improved symptomatology; there was a numerical but non-significant reduction in AF burden. This pilot study sets the stage for future pivotal trials of MNS in AF patients.

candidates.title: Interventricular septal LGE predicts response trajectories and clinical prognosis in heart failure patients undergoing left bundle branch area pacing.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is an alternative strategy for heart failure (HF) patients with left bundle branch block (LBBB). Interventricular septal (IVS) fibrosis is linked to LBBAP efficacy.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between IVS late gadolinium enhancement percentage (IVS LGE%) and LBBAP response in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) patients with LBBB.
METHODS: This was a two-center prospective observational study. Patients with NICM and complete LBBB were consecutively enrolled and received LBBAP from January 2021 to December 2024. Patients were divided into early, delayed, and non-response groups based on absolute left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement ≥5% at 6 and 12 months.
RESULTS: A total of 113 patients were included, with 86 (76.1%) early responders, 13 (11.5%) delayed responders, and 14 (12.4%) non-responders. IVS LGE% linearly increased the risk of non-early response, with each 1% increase conferring a 14% higher risk of adverse response progression (early to delayed or non-response) (adjusted OR=1.14, 95%CI 1.05-1.23; P=0.002). 75.3% of IVS fibrosis-related 6-month impairment was mediated by failed LBB captured (direct effect P=0.204), while the direct inhibitory effect of IVS fibrosis emerged at 12 months (mediation proportion 60.8%, β=-0.33, P=0.005). Optimal IVS LGE% cut-off values were 7.62% for early response and 12.33% for delayed response, with 12-month response rates of 95.06%, 93.75% and 43.75% across low, intermediate and high IVS LGE% groups, respectively.
CONCLUSION: IVS fibrosis independently predicts LBBAP response and prognosis in NICM patients with complete LBBB, and modulates LBBAP efficacy through a time-dependent biphasic mechanism.

candidates.title: Effect of telemedicine-based integrated management of atrial fibrillation in village clinics on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events: a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an increasing public health challenge, particularly among rural older adults, where awareness and treatment remain inadequate. While the MIRACLE-AF trial demonstrated that telemedicine-based, village doctor-led integrated care reduced cardiovascular mortality or first major cardiovascular events, its impact on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events remains unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of the MIRACLE-AF care model on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial (NCT04622514), a cluster-randomized controlled trial enrolling 1,039 rural patients aged ≥65 years with confirmed AF across 30 village clinics over 36 months. Village clinics were randomized 1:1 to village doctor-led telemedicine integrated care or enhanced usual care. The primary outcome was recurrent nonfatal events over 36 months, including strokes, hospitalizations for worsening heart failure or acute coronary syndrome, and emergency visits for AF, analyzed using a conditional frailty model.
RESULTS: Among 1039 patients (mean age 75.8 ± 5.7 years; 44.3% female), the intervention experienced fewer cardiovascular events than the control (118 events in 82 patients [15.65%] vs. 173 events in 122 patients [23.69%]). The observed recurrent event rates were 6.75 and 9.11 per 100 patient-years, respectively. The estimated hazard ratio was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.583-1.004; p = 0.053), indicating that the difference did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSION: Although the overall difference did not reach statistical significance, directional trends consistently favored telemedicine-based integrated care, suggesting a potential reduction in recurrent cardiovascular event burden. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

candidates.title: Sex-based differences in bi-atrial voltage in atrial fibrillation: a multimodal and digital twin approach to distinguish physiological variation from pathological remodelling.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex-based differences in atrial voltage have been reported in atrial fibrillation (AF), but it is unclear whether these differences reflect pathological remodelling or physiological variation.
OBJECTIVE: To assess sex-based differences in voltage, contextualised by complementary measures of substrate remodelling and AF mechanisms.
METHODS: A multicentre, prospective study was conducted in patients scheduled for AF ablation. Bi-atrial voltage mapping was combined with electrophysiological assessment, structural and functional assessment using cardiac MRI, and mechanistic interrogation using patient-specific digital twins. Propensity score matching was used to account for baseline differences between sexes. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis was conducted to estimate sex-specific mean left atrial voltage cutoffs based on 12-month arrhythmia recurrence status.
RESULTS: Seventy patients (62±12 years; 31% female) were included. Women demonstrated lower mean bipolar voltages than men, with this difference persisting after 1:1 propensity score matching (n=44) in both left (1.66±0.71mV versus 2.12±0.55mV, p=0.028) and right atria (1.79±0.49mV versus 2.20±0.59mV, p=0.025). Propensity score-matched analyses revealed no significant differences in other structural, functional, or electrophysiological parameters, with digital twin analyses demonstrating no significant differences in AF termination, phase singularity count, wave dynamics, or response to virtual ablation. Women had lower mean left atrial voltage cutoffs calibrated to 12-month arrhythmia recurrence status than men (1.74mV versus 2.26mV).
CONCLUSIONS: Women with AF exhibit lower bi-atrial voltages despite comparable substrate characteristics and AF mechanisms, suggesting that observed voltage differences may reflect physiological variation rather than pathological remodelling. Sex-specific voltage thresholds may improve the accuracy of substrate assessment and facilitate personalised treatment.

candidates.title: Atrial Fibrillation Pattern and Outcomes After Contemporary Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) pattern predicts thromboembolic risk during anticoagulation, but its prognostic importance after left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether AF pattern independently predicts residual clinical risk after contemporary LAAO and whether peri-device leak (PDL) or device-related thrombus (DRT) identify a persistently high-risk subgroup.
METHODS: We studied 3,459 patients with documented AF pattern undergoing LAAO in a contemporary multicenter registry. AF was classified as paroxysmal, persistent or long-standing persistent, or permanent. The primary endpoint was a 2-year hierarchical composite of death, stroke or systemic embolism (stroke/SE), and major bleeding analyzed by win ratio. Inverse probability weighting and propensity score methods adjusted for baseline differences. Follow-up imaging assessed PDL and DRT.
RESULTS: After inverse probability weighting, persistent and permanent AF were associated with progressively worse hierarchical outcomes compared with paroxysmal AF (win ratios 1.39 and 1.59, respectively). Non-paroxysmal AF was associated with higher stroke risk (HR 1.64; 95% CI 1.07-2.50), without increased mortality or major bleeding. PDL and DRT were more frequent in non-paroxysmal AF. In the PDL/DRT subgroup, non-paroxysmal AF was associated with higher first stroke/SE risk (HR 1.83; 95% CI 1.00-3.34), concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO.
CONCLUSIONS: AF pattern independently stratified residual clinical risk after LAAO, with progressively worse severity-weighted outcomes from paroxysmal to persistent and permanent AF. Excess risk was driven primarily by thromboembolism. In the PDL/DRT subgroup, the association was concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO, suggesting these patients may benefit from prolonged thromboembolic surveillance.

candidates.title: Pulmonary vein narrowing after voltage-guided adjunctive pulmonary vein sleeve pulsed field ablation.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) for pulmonary vein (PV) isolation (PVI) has been associated with a low risk of PV stenosis when performed using the standard ostial workflow. However, the risk of PV narrowing after adjunctive PV sleeve PFA remains insufficiently evaluated.
OBJECTIVE: To assess PV narrowing after voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve PFA.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 147 patients who underwent an initial pentaspline PFA-based PVI for atrial fibrillation. In addition to standard ostial PVI, voltage-guided PFA applications were delivered to target PV sleeve potentials identified on pre-ablation voltage mapping. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography was performed before and approximately six months after ablation. PV cross-sectional areas (PVAs) were measured at predefined levels, and the maximum PVA reduction rate was defined as ΔPVA. Significant PV narrowing was defined as ΔPVA ≥25%.
RESULTS: Post-ablation PVA was significantly smaller than pre-ablation PVA at all PV sites. The median ΔPVA was 5.4%, 6.4%, 4.6%, and 4.0% in the left superior, left inferior, right superior, and right inferior PVs, respectively, and differed significantly among the four PV sites (P = 0.012). No significant PV narrowing was observed in this cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing an initial PFA-based PVI, no significant PV narrowing was observed approximately six months after voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve PFA using a pentaspline catheter. Further controlled studies with larger populations and longer follow-up are needed to better characterize the safety and clinical utility of this strategy.

candidates.title: Prognostic Impact of Ventricular Arrhythmia Timing in Acute Coronary Syndromes Treated with Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular arrhythmias (VA) often complicate acute coronary syndromes (ACS). The prognostic impact of VA timing relative to percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prognostic significance of VA based on their timing of occurrence in relation to PCI.
METHODS: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies reporting all-cause mortality with and without VA (sustained or hemodynamically unstable VT/VF) in ACS patients undergoing PCI. The endpoints analyzed were short-term (30 days/in-hospital) and long-term (1 year) mortality. A network meta-analysis comparing VA-before PCI, VA-during PCI, and VA-after PCI with the group not experiencing VA as a reference was conducted.
RESULTS: Twelve studies comprising 49,963 patients were included, of whom 3,475 (7.0%) experienced VA. VA was associated with increased short- (OR 5.04, 95%CI 3.78-6.72) and long-term mortality (OR 2.92, 95%CI 2.20-3.86). In patients alive at discharge/30 days, subsequent long-term mortality risk did not differ between those with and without VA (OR 0.97, 95%CI 0.62-1.52). The network meta-analysis showed that all VA timings are associated with a significantly higher risk compared with the group not experiencing VA. Sensitivity analysis found that VA-after is associated with higher short-term mortality than earlier VA (OR 3.37, 95%CI 1.46-7.82).
CONCLUSIONS: VA substantially increase the risk of death in patients with ACS undergoing PCI. Mortality risk emerges to be associated with the timing of VA occurrence, with VA-after PCI associated with the highest risk. These findings highlight the prognostic relevance of arrhythmic events across the entire peri-procedural window, underscoring the need for refined risk stratification.

candidates.title: Day-Night Patterns of Wearable-Derived Electrocardiographic Age and Left Atrial Remodeling in Atrial Fibrillation-Naïve Individuals.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence-derived electrocardiographic (AI-ECG) age is conventionally treated as a static marker. Its diurnal dynamics and structural correlates in individuals without atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize diurnal AI-ECG age patterns, their reproducibility, and associations with left atrial (LA) remodeling.
METHODS: We analyzed continuous wearable ECGs from two prospective registries (NCT05119725, NCT05355948). In 499 AF-naïve participants with ≥48-hour recordings, AI-ECG age was estimated every 10 minutes. Unsupervised clustering identified day-night trajectories, summarized by day-night difference (ΔAge) into Restorative (>0.6 years) or Disrupted (≤0.6 years) phenotypes. Reproducibility was evaluated across sequential periods. Age- and sex-adjusted associations of binary and continuous ΔAge with LA volume index (LAVI) were pooled in a cross-sectional echocardiographic substudy (n=122).
RESULTS: Three trajectories emerged in both registries. Restorative prevalence was 47.6%-50.2%. Agreement between two consecutive 48-hour periods was 75.8% (κ = 0.516; 95% CI, 0.395-0.631); 6- to 8-day intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.51-0.54. The Disrupted phenotype was associated with higher LAVI (pooled mean difference, 5.54 mL/m2; 95% CI, 1.11-9.98; P = .014) and greater odds of LA enlargement (LAVI ≥40 mL/m2; pooled odds ratio, 3.68; 95% CI, 1.45-9.29; P = .006). Per 1-SD higher ΔAge, LAVI was lower (β, -2.89 mL/m2; P = .007) and LA enlargement less likely (odds ratio, 0.53; P = .004).
CONCLUSION: Wearable-derived AI-ECG age exhibits a reproducible day-night pattern. A Disrupted phenotype is associated with adverse LA remodeling. Because reproducibility remains insufficient for individual-level classification, prospective outcome-based validation is warranted.

candidates.title: Ten-year Performance of the Multi-Layer Insulated Defibrillation Lead in the Medicare Population.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term surveillance of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads is essential because clinically important mechanical failures may emerge years after implantation.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate 10-year mechanical complication-free survival of the Optisure ICD lead (Abbott, Sylmar, CA) in a large real-world Medicare population.
METHODS: Manufacturer device-tracking records were linked to Medicare Fee-for-Service claims and device complaint data using the EP PASSION framework. Patients receiving an Optisure lead from February 2014 through December 2024 were included. Mechanical lead-related complications were defined by claims containing both a diagnosis of mechanical lead malfunction and a lead-related surgical intervention more than 30 days after implantation. Kaplan-Meier survival was estimated under a best-case scenario including confirmed Optisure-related events and a worst-case scenario also including potentially related events.
RESULTS: The cohort included 26,830 patients with 27,033 Optisure leads. Mean age was 73.8 ± 8.6 years, 28.4% were women, and 49.8% had cardiac resynchronization therapy ICDs. Overall, 379 complications were classified as confirmed lead-related and 606 as confirmed or potentially lead-related. At 10 years, complication-free lead survival was 97.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 96.7%-97.7%) in the best-case scenario and 95.6% (95% CI, 94.9%-96.2%) in the worst-case scenario. Survival did not differ significantly by age, lead length, coil configuration, or device type.
CONCLUSION: The Optisure ICD lead demonstrated favorable mechanical performance through 10 years in routine clinical practice. These findings support both the long-term durability of Optisure and the use of integrated real-world data for post-market device surveillance.

candidates.title: Epicardial Closure for Peridevice Leaks from Endocardial Left Atrial Appendage Closure - Early LARIAT-4-PDL Registry Results.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Closure of clinically significant peri-device leaks (PDLs) after left atrial appendage (LAA) occlusion remains crucial to prevent thromboembolism. A variety of techniques exist to close PDLs, each with its own advantages and disadvantages. The LARIAT (Atricure, Mason, OH) suture device may provide an alternative for closing PDLs.
OBJECTIVE: We report the initial feasibility of LARIAT for endocardial LAA closure PDLs.
METHODS: In a multicenter, retrospective study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent LARIAT for closure of device-related LAA leaks. All patients had PDLs ≥3 mm after either a Watchman FLX Pro (Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA) or an Amplatzer Amulet (Abbott, Chicago, IL) endocardial LAA occluder, as seen on postoperative imaging. Acute PDL closure - pericardial access with device deployment and elimination of the PDL on intraprocedural imaging - was evaluated with either transesophageal or intracardiac echocardiogram, along with 45-day safety.
RESULTS: We report 10 cases in patients aged 67.2±10.7years, 30.0% female, and with a body mass index 32.4±6.4 kg/m2. Baseline comorbidities included a CHADSVASC of 4.4±0.7 and HASBLED of 3.7±0.7. Initially, patients underwent Watchman (80.0%) or Amulet (20.0%) with an average PDL of 5.4±0.8 mm. Few cases had attempted PDL closure with radiofrequency ablation (10.0%), coiling (20.0%), or a previous device (10.0%). After procedural and fluoroscopy times of 48.7±10.8 min and 7.0±3.7 min, respectively, LARIAT PDL closure was successful in all cases, and no difference when stratified by initial endocardial LAA closure type.
CONCLUSION: These initial results suggest that a LARIAT may be an alternative strategy in patients with clinically significant PDLs after endocardial LAA closure. Future studies are needed to corroborate our initial findings and long-term closure results.

candidates.title: Dose-Response Associations of Exercise Modalities With Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Exercise training improves cardiorespiratory fitness in patients with heart failure, yet the dose-response relationship across different exercise modalities remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different exercise modalities and their standardized doses on peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak) in patients with heart failure.
METHODS: We systematically searched multiple databases from inception through March 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing exercise interventions with controls. Exercise modalities were categorized as interval aerobic training (IAT), continuous aerobic training (CAT), resistance training (RT), mind-body training (MBT), and their combinations. Exercise dose was uniformly quantified as weekly metabolic equivalents (MET-min/week). A Bayesian model-based network dose-response meta-analysis was performed.
RESULTS: A total of 100 trials involving 5,353 patients were included. The dose-response relationship followed an Emax curve, with ED50 values clustering around 80-90 MET-min/week. A weekly dose of 500 MET-min yielded considerable benefit, and 750-1000 MET-min approached maximal benefit for nearly all modalities. The top three ranked interventions were IAT (Emax = 3.50, 95% CrI: 2.49-4.60), RT (Emax = 3.66, 95% CrI: 1.96-5.85), and IAT+RT (Emax = 3.49, 95% CrI: 1.26-5.79).
CONCLUSIONS: The exercise dose-response relationship in heart failure follows an Emax curve, with distinct dose-benefit profiles across different exercise modalities. Based on the current evidence, the following preliminary considerations may be offered: for patients with limited exercise tolerance, MBT may be considered as one of the preferred options; for those with moderate exercise tolerance, IAT+RT or CAT+RT may be suitable choices; for patients with good exercise tolerance, IAT or RT may be considered; and for patients with comorbid obesity, CAT may be incorporated into a comprehensive management program.

candidates.title: Short-term safety, feasibility, and performance of a novel soft robotic biventricular mechanical circulatory support device avoiding blood contact - The MISSION reBEAT trial.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Mechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) remains limited in advanced heart failure due to blood-contact complications and the absence of biventricular support. We report the first prospective clinical trial of a novel soft-robotic, biventricular, pulsatile technology placed externally around the heart without blood contact, designed to deliver individualized cardiac assistance (reBEAT®, AdjuCor GmbH, Munich, Germany).
METHODS AND RESULTS: The system was temporarily applied in 10 end-stage heart failure patients immediately before elective LVAD implantation. Devices were custom-manufactured using preoperative CT scans to match individual cardiac anatomy. Safety, feasibility, and effects on haemodynamics were evaluated. Implantation was rapid (3±2 min), demonstrating procedural feasibility. We observed two procedure-related adverse events while no device- or procedure-related severe adverse events occurred. Absence of new ECG abnormalities, and no tissue injury confirmed safety. An iterative assessment on haemodynamics provided key insights into individualized cardio-circulatory support. While device presence reduced preload dependent haemodynamics in some patients, low average support pressures of 65-66 mmHg produced variable improvements towards baseline, predominantly on the pressure signal: mean arterial pressure (MAP; 67.5 ± 10.6 vs. 76.2 ± 11.7 mmHg, p<0.01), stroke work (SW; 347.8 ± 118.2 vs. 434.1 ± 131.0 mJ, p<0.01), and cardiac power output (CPO; 407.9 ± 108.2 vs. 503.7 ± 116.2 mW, p<0.01). Additionally, effects were observed on atrioventricular valve function and interventricular balance, which were not significant.
CONCLUSION: This soft-robotic biventricular MCS platform provides short term evidence of a safe and feasible approach to pulsatile biventricular support without blood contact. Significant increases in MAP, CPO, and SW towards baseline indicate functional effects. Continuous device-driven workflow improvement is mandatory and further data are required to refine individualized optimization strategies. This technology may offer a novel biventricular assist modality. Its reduced complexity may enable broader adaption for both temporary and durable support. Avoiding blood contact and enabling balanced biventricular assistance will be central drivers of its continued clinical development.

candidates.title: Advanced Subclinical Atherosclerosis in Young Individuals and Risk of Mortality Over 30 Years: The Coronary Artery Calcium Consortium.
candidates.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring is a well-established tool for predicting cardiovascular risk, but its long-term prognostic value in young adults remains unclear. As early preventive intervention may yield substantial lifetime benefit, understanding long-term implications of elevated CAC in young adults is important for informing prevention strategies.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the long-term risk of all-cause, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and coronary heart disease (CHD) mortality associated with premature advanced subclinical atherosclerosis.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used the CAC Consortium dataset, a retrospectively assembled cohort of referred individuals with clinically indicated CAC scans. Using multivariable regression models for time-to-event analysis, the association of CAC with all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality was assessed, adjusting for age, sex, and traditional atherosclerotic CVD risk factors. Cumulative incidence was derived for these outcomes in 5-year increments up to 30 years using a mixed approach involving the Kaplan-Meier method and Weibull modeling. The proportion of deaths attributable to CVD and CHD across CAC groups was evaluated. Four institutions across the US provided patient-level data to assemble the CAC Consortium. Included in the analysis were adults aged 30 to 45 years from the CAC Consortium. They were followed up for a median of 22.6 years. Study data were analyzed from October 2025 to September 2026.
EXPOSURE: Elevated CAC in adults aged 30 to 45 years, specifically CAC score greater than 90%.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Participants were followed up for underlying cause of mortality.
RESULTS: Among 12 847 participants, the mean (SD) age was 40.5 (3.6) years, and 9922 (77.2%) were male; 9262 (72.1%) had CAC score of 0, 1626 (12.7%) had a CAC score between 75% to 90%, and 1703 (13.3%) had a CAC score greater than 90%. In total, there were 624 deaths (149 CVD and 81 CHD). Multivariable adjusted hazard ratios for CAC score greater than 90% vs CAC score of 0 were 1.87 (95% CI, 1.54-2.27), 2.60 (95% CI, 1.77-3.82), and 3.71 (95% CI, 2.24-6.16), for all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality, respectively. Over 30 years, the group with a CAC score greater than 90% had significantly higher modeled risk of all-cause (12.9% vs 7.5%), CVD (4.5% vs 1.5%), and CHD (3.0% vs 0.6%) mortality, compared with the group with a CAC score of 0.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this cohort study suggest that young adults with a CAC score greater than 90% face significantly higher long-term risk of all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality, suggesting potential implications for guiding the intensification of preventive intervention in this high-risk phenotype.

candidates.title: Pacing Related Conduction Delay as an Indicator of Intramural Site of Origin of Focal Ventricular Arrhythmias.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The diagnosis of intramural focal ventricular arrhythmias (VA) can be challenging and is often made in retrospect after a long ineffective procedure.
OBJECTIVES: In this cohort of patients, we aim to assess the value of pace-mapping (PM), stimulus-QRS interval (S-QRS interval), and electrogram (EGM)-QRS intervals to identify the site of origin (SOO) of focal VAs.
METHODS: In a consecutive series of 46 patients with frequent premature ventricular complexes (PVCs), activation mapping and PM were performed to identify VA target sites. VA target sites were defined as sites with matching PM (≥10/12 leads) and/or sites with the earliest activation time. S-QRS interval and bipolar activation time at target sites were assessed and correlated with acute outcomes. If ablation at a target site failed, alternative sites were sought in adjacent anatomical structures. An intramural origin was defined as a VA with early activation time without a matching PM.
RESULTS: Matching PMs were identified for 32 VAs in 30 of the 46 patients. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was performed at the target site/PVC level and demonstrated that a mismatch between S-QRS and EGM-QRS of >26 milliseconds distinguished effective from ineffective ablation sites with a matching PM (area under the curve: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.94-1; sensitivity: 100%; specificity: 88.9%). A mismatch was present in 9 patients, and radiofrequency ablation failed in 8/9 of them. Alternate sites with early activation times (-48.4 ± 37.39 milliseconds) without matching PM, where radiofrequency eliminated the PVCs, were identified in 5/8 patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Conduction delay with matching PMs but late activation indicates a deeper SOO. A cutoff value of >26 milliseconds between S-QRS and EGM-QRS intervals identified deeper-seated VA target sites. This required further mapping to identify alternative ablation sites. A matching PM may not always be indicative of the SOO in patients with PVCs.

candidates.title: Safety and Outcomes of Transvenous Lead Extraction of Advisory ePTFE-Coated Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Leads: A Multicenter Experience With RELIANCE G.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE)-coated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads are associated with progressive coil calcification and rising shock impedance, prompting a recent safety advisory. However, data regarding the safety and efficacy of transvenous lead extraction (TLE) for these chronic leads remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and procedural outcomes of TLE in patients with advisory ePTFE-coated ICD leads.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter study at 13 centers of patients undergoing TLE of ePTFE-coated ICD leads. Primary endpoints included procedural success, complications, and short-term mortality. Multivariable analyses identified predictors of outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 423 patients undergoing extraction of advisory RELIANCE ICD leads (Boston Scientific), mean lead dwell time was 7.5 ± 5.3 years, and impedance-defined coil calcification was present in 15.1%. Laser sheaths were used in 63.8% of procedures and multiple extraction tools in 21.7%. Complete lead removal was achieved in 95.5%, clinical success in 98.8%, and extraction failed occurred in 1.2%. Major complications occurred in 0.9% of patients, with no procedural deaths. Calcified leads were associated with longer dwell times but not higher rates of major complications. Thirty-day mortality was 2.8%, primarily among patients undergoing extraction for infection.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large multicenter cohort, TLE of advisory ePTFE-coated ICD leads was associated with high procedural success and low major complication rates despite long lead dwell times. Outcomes were consistent with contemporary TLE experience and do not suggest increased procedural risk attributable to this lead model. The presence of impedance-defined coil calcification did not adversely affect procedural outcomes, supporting TLE at experienced centers when clinically indicated.

candidates.title: Bromocriptine for Myocardial Recovery in Peripartum Cardiomyopathy: Design and Rationale of the REBIRTH Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is evidence suggesting that bromocriptine potentially improves outcomes among women with peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM); however, there is currently no randomized controlled trial comparing bromocriptine vs placebo on top of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in a diverse, multiethnic cohort in North America.
OBJECTIVES: The REBIRTH trial will enroll 200 women with PPCM to evaluate whether the addition of oral bromocriptine to GDMT is superior to placebo for improving myocardial function and event-free survival. In addition to the randomized trial, REBIRTH will enroll 50 women with PPCM excluded from randomization because of breastfeeding into an observational cohort.
METHODS: The principal inclusion criteria are ≥18 years of age, within 5-months postpartum, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤40%. The primary endpoint is LVEF at 6 months postrandomization. Secondary endpoints include LVEF at 12 months, survival free from major events (ie, death, heart transplantation, or implantation of a durable left ventricular assist device), and survival free from heart failure hospitalization for up to 3 years.
RESULTS: The study is currently enrolling women in both the randomized trial and observational breastfeeding cohort. Primary results are expected to be reported in 2027.
CONCLUSIONS: REBIRTH will determine whether the addition of bromocriptine to GDMT for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction improves postpartum myocardial recovery and clinical outcomes in a diverse cohort of women with PPCM. (Randomized Evaluation of Bromocriptine in Myocardial Recovery Therapy for PPCM [REBIRTH]; NCT05180773).

candidates.title: Safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism: the SPIRARE II pivotal trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy can rapidly reduce afterload in acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but catheter stiffness and instability may limit access and prevent effective right ventricle (RV) unloading. The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System with Transforming Fixation (TFX) technology is designed to address current limitations of existing catheter-based systems by separating the flexibility necessary for safe navigation from the support that is essential for procedural control.
AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE.
METHODS: SPIRARE II was a prospective, single-arm, multicentre pivotal investigation conducted at 19 sites in the United States and Europe. Eligible patients had acute PE (≤14 days), a computed tomography angiography-assessed RV to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio>0.9, and haemodynamic stability (systolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg). Co-primary endpoints were composite major adverse events (MAE) within 48 hours and core laboratory-assessed RV/LV change from baseline to 48 hours. Prespecified secondary endpoints were collected immediately pre- and post-procedure in all patients including mean pulmonary artery pressure, total pulmonary vascular resistance, and cardiac index.
RESULTS: In 123 patients, the 48-hour composite MAE rate was 2.4% (3/123), meeting the prespecified performance goal (one-sided p<0.0001). The mean RV/LV diameter ratio decreased from 1.44±0.33 at baseline to 1.05±0.21 at 48 hours, a mean reduction of 0.39±0.33, exceeding the prespecified performance goal (p<0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System met its prespecified safety and effectiveness endpoints in acute intermediate-risk PE. TFX delivered precise, stable control with reliable vessel access, enabling consistent right ventricular unloading. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06576427).

candidates.title: Coronary artery disease management in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal management of coronary artery disease in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain.
AIMS: We aimed to compare clinical outcomes between routine coronary revascularisation and conservative management in patients undergoing TAVI and to assess the relative effectiveness of individual revascularisation strategies by performing a meta-analysis of randomised trials.
METHODS: We conducted a pairwise meta-analysis comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with conservative treatment and a network meta-analysis comparing the relative effectiveness of individual strategies, including angiography-guided and physiology-guided PCI. The primary outcome was a study-defined composite endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included the individual outcomes of all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unplanned revascularisation, and major bleeding.
RESULTS: Five trials (N=1,644 patients) were included in the systematic review, and four were included in the primary quantitative synthesis (N=1,476). Compared with conservative treatment, routine PCI was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio [RR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.83) and an increased risk of major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32). In the network meta-analysis, physiology-guided PCI significantly reduced MACE, stroke, and unplanned revascularisation compared with conservative treatment and ranked highest for all ischaemic outcomes among revascularisation strategies.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients referred for TAVI, routine revascularisation reduces the risk of ischaemic outcomes compared with conservative treatment. In this setting, physiology-guided PCI may be associated with the most favourable efficacy profile across available strategies. (PROSPERO: CRD420261330194).

candidates.title: Sirolimus-Coated Balloon Angioplasty for Femoropopliteal Artery Disease Without Tissue Loss: A Secondary Analysis of the SirPAD Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty performs better than uncoated balloon angioplasty among patients with exertional symptoms due to femoropopliteal artery disease remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to describe 1-year outcomes after sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty among participants in the SirPAD (Sirolimus-Coated Balloon for Peripheral Artery Disease) trial with femoropopliteal artery disease.
METHODS: In this analysis of the multicenter, randomized, blinded-endpoint SirPAD trial, we evaluated outcomes for patients with femoropopliteal target lesions and without tissue loss (Rutherford category ≤4, Fontaine stage ≤III). A secondary subgroup was restricted to patients with a lower disease burden, excluding ischemic rest pain, prior major amputation, or below-the-knee revascularization. We compared the 1-year rate of: 1) target-lesion revascularization (TLR); 2) the composite of TLR and any unplanned amputation; 3) major adverse limb events; and 4) all-cause death.
RESULTS: Among 597 patients, median age was 71 years, 34.7% were women, and median target-lesion length was 150 mm; 53.8% had total occlusion. After 1 year, 50 patients (17.0%) had undergone TLR in the sirolimus-coated balloon group vs 82 (27.1%) among control subjects (absolute risk difference [ARD]: -10.1%; 95% CI: -16.6 to -3.0). Any amputation or any TLR occurred in 17.7% and 27.1% of patients respectively (ARD: -9.4%; 95% CI: -16.0 to -2.7). Major adverse limb events occurred in 4.1% vs 8.9% of patients, respectively (ARD: -4.8%; 95% CI: -9.0 to -0.8). One-year all-cause death was similar (3.7% vs 5.3%).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with femoropopliteal artery disease and no tissue loss, sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty was associated with a lower 1-year rate of TLR compared with uncoated balloon angioplasty. These findings are descriptive rather than confirmatory. (Sirolimus-Coated Balloon for Peripheral Artery Disease; NCT04238546).

candidates.title: Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy Using a Conduction System Pacing Defibrillation Lead in Patients Meeting CRT-D Indications: Six-Month Clinical Outcomes Results From the ASCEND CSP Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) via left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is a physiologic alternative to conventional biventricular (BiV) pacing for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), but prospective data using purpose-built implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads are limited.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate procedural success, defibrillation efficacy, safety, and 6-month clinical outcomes of left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy (LOT-CRT) delivered with a purpose-built CSP ICD lead and compare outcomes to conventional BiV-CRT.
METHODS: A total of 52 CRT defibrillator patients (age 66 ± 10 years, 31.4% female, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) 29.5 ± 6.7%, left bundle branch block [LBBB] 66.7%, QRSd 164.6 ± 25.3 milliseconds, 29.4% ischemic) in the ASCEND CSP IDE (A Stylet-Driven ICD Lead Intended for Conduction System Pacing IDE Study) study underwent attempted implantation of a CSP ICD lead and a coronary sinus lead (LOT-CRT). Implant success, safety and efficacy outcomes, electrocardiographic characteristics, echocardiographic remodeling, heart failure status, patient-reported quality of life, and CRT response were assessed through 6 months. Outcomes were compared with a propensity-matched conventional CRT cohort (BiV-CRT).
RESULTS: Implantation succeeded in 98.1% (51 of 52), with LBBAP capture achieved in all (51 of 51). Freedom from CSP lead-related serious adverse device effects through 6 months was 98.1% (95% CI: 87.1%-99.7%). Defibrillation was successful in all tested patients (100%). Compared with baseline, QRS narrowed by 30.4 ms and LVEF increased by 10.4 points (both P < 0.0001), with a CRT response (≥5%) in 71.1% and super-response (≥14.5%) in 34.2%. Compared with matched BiV-CRT patients from the MORE-CRT MPP (MORE response on Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy with MultiPoint Pacing) study, lead-related events were similar (2.0% vs 2.5%; P = 1.0), LVEF increase was greater (10.4 points vs 4.6 points; P = 0.0005) with more responders (≥5%) and super-responders (≥14.5%) (71.1% vs 48.5%; P = 0.0107 and 34.2% vs 7.8%; P < 0.0001, respectively), and more patients improved by clinical composite score (76.5% vs 52.0%; P = 0.0016). Significant improvements were seen with LOT-CRT in both LBBB and non-LBBB patients.
CONCLUSIONS: LOT-CRT with a dedicated CSP ICD lead achieved high implant success, preserved defibrillation efficacy, and had favorable safety, with greater left ventricular systolic function and clinical improvement than matched conventional CRT, supporting CSP-based CRT defibrillator therapy.

candidates.title: Cardiac Structure and Function in Women After Preeclampsia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia increases the risk of long-term heart failure (HF) by 4-fold. Unfortunately, however, universal guidelines for postpartum HF surveillance are lacking. Stage B/subclinical HF has been shown to predict risk of major adverse cardiac outcomes. Some suggest that initiating cardioprotective therapy at this early stage can reduce progression to symptomatic HF.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this review was to explore cardiac structure and function in women with a history of preeclampsia and to identify when subclinical HF develops in this group.
METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, EMBASE and CINAHL was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines to identify all studies assessing left ventricular function on transthoracic echocardiography in women with a history of preeclampsia.
RESULTS: A total of 45 case-control studies comprising 8,991 women, including 2,288 women with a history of preeclampsia, were included in the final analysis. During pregnancy, women with preeclampsia had a higher left ventricular mass index (LVMI) (standard mean difference: 10.85 [95% CI: 6.30-15.39]), relative wall thickness (0.05 [95% CI: 0.03-0.08]), E/e' (1.58 [95% CI: 1.02-2.13]), isovolumetric relaxation time (8.74 [95% CI: 3.14-14.34]), lower E/A ratio (-0.27 [95% CI: -0.51 to -0.04]) and reduced absolute global longitudinal strain (GLS) values (2.27 [95% CI: 0.43-4.11]), indicating reduced myocardial function compared with normotensive controls. Postpartum, GLS remained reduced, and LVMI remained elevated in women with a history of preeclampsia. This difference persisted out to 10 years postpartum. There was no significant difference in all other variables >6 months postpartum. Evidence for persistent LVMI elevation >6 months postpartum was not robust in sensitivity analyses excluding overlapping cohorts. Left ventricular ejection fraction and right ventricular function remained similar in the preeclampsia and control groups throughout.
CONCLUSIONS: Preeclampsia is associated with subclinical myocardial dysfunction, characterized by impaired GLS and increased LVMI. Persistent impairment in GLS was observed up to 10 years postpartum, whereas the association with elevated LVMI beyond 6 months postpartum should be interpreted with caution. Further studies are required to assess when subclinical myocardial dysfunction progresses to symptomatic clinical HF.

candidates.title: Three ablation strategies using very high-power short-duration catheter in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: The Q-INDEX randomized trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Very high-power short-duration (vHPSD; 90 W/4 sec) ablation shortens pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) but produces shallower lesions that may be inadequate in the thick anterior left atrium.
OBJECTIVE: To compare vHPSD, ablation index (AI)-guided, and hybrid strategies for PVI in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, open-label trial, 150 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation were assigned 1:1:1 with the QDOT MICRO catheter to (1) AI-guided (AI 500 anterior, 400 elsewhere), (2) hybrid (AI-guided anterior [AI 500], vHPSD elsewhere), or (3) vHPSD (90 W/4 sec, all segments). The primary endpoint was total ablation time; secondary endpoints included acute PV reconnection, safety, and 1-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia.
RESULTS: Acute PVI was achieved in all patients. Total ablation time was longest with AI-guided and shortest with vHPSD ablation (median 2220 vs 1450 vs 794 sec; P < .001). Acute reconnection across the 14 PV segments was lowest with AI-guided and highest with vHPSD (7.7% vs 9.4% vs 10.6%; P = .40). One-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia was 92.0%, 85.4%, and 77.6%, respectively (log-rank P = .13; for AI-guided vs vHPSD; P = .049). No tamponade occurred; steam pops occurred only in the 90 W groups. Two minor periprocedural strokes occurred (both vHPSD; full recovery), and silent cerebral lesions on magnetic resonance imaging did not differ among the groups (5%, 10%, 0%; P = .35).
CONCLUSION: Uniform vHPSD more than halved PVI ablation time but was associated with the lowest 1-year efficacy, whereas the hybrid strategy preserved efficiency without significant loss of durability. These exploratory findings-from a trial powered for ablation time-support region-tailored lesion depth in point-by-point ablation and warrant confirmation.

candidates.title: Feasibility and Restenosis Predictors of Optical Frequency Domain Imaging-Guided Drug-Coated Balloon Treatment for Femoropopliteal Lesions.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical utility of optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) for guiding endovascular therapy in femoropopliteal lesions has not been established. Additionally, the prognostic value of OFDI findings during drug-coated balloon (DCB) treatment for femoropopliteal lesions has never been evaluated.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to clarify the feasibility of OFDI-guided DCB treatment and investigate the OFDI findings associated with restenosis after DCB treatment in femoropopliteal lesions.
METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, observational study included patients with symptomatic, nonseverely calcified femoropopliteal lesions who underwent DCB treatment under OFDI guidance. Procedural success was defined as residual stenosis of less than 30% without flow compromise and without any procedural complications. The primary outcome was restenosis of the target lesion, defined as a peak systolic velocity ratio of ≥2.5, as measured by duplex ultrasound at rest or target lesion revascularization.
RESULTS: A total of 202 lesions were initially enrolled, of which 35 (17.3%) were excluded primarily because of severe calcification or inadequate OFDI data. Among the 167 analyzable lesions included in the present analysis, the procedural success rate and 1-year freedom from restenosis were 91.6% and 85.5%, respectively. In the procedural OFDI findings, a calcified nodule in the target lesion (subdistribution hazard ratio: 3.25; 95% CI: 1.01-10.42; P = 0.048) was associated with restenosis.
CONCLUSIONS: OFDI-guided DCB treatment is feasible in selected femoropopliteal lesions. An OFDI-detected calcified nodule is associated with an increased risk of restenosis after DCB treatment for femoropopliteal lesions.

candidates.title: Effectiveness of digital health interventions for care integration in coronary artery disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
candidates.abstract:
AIM: To assess the effectiveness of digital health interventions (DHIs) supporting care integration for coronary artery disease (CAD) in improving health outcomes compared to usual care.
METHODS: For this systematic review, we searched MEDLINE, CINAHL, EBSCO Psychology and Behavioural Sciences Collection, Scopus, and Web of Science from 1 January 1995 to 5 November 2025. We included studies reporting primary data on DHIs supporting care integration for patients with CAD. Primary endpoints were all-cause mortality and readmissions, and CVD events. Secondary endpoints were the control of cardiovascular risk factors. We conducted random-effects meta-analyses in RevMan and assessed risk of bias with Cochrane's RoB tools.
RESULTS: We included 72 studies (23,111 participants), assessing 45 in the meta-analysis. All DHIs supported person-centred care integration (n=72) while few DHIs addressed clinical care integration (n=22), professional integration (n=12) and functional integration (n=22). Compared to usual care, DHIs supporting care integration had significant reductions in the odds of CVD events (OR: 0.74 [0.59, 0.92], df=5, p=0.02), but not in all-cause mortality or readmissions.
CONCLUSIONS: Although this review shows that DHIs supporting care integration were associated with reduced CVD events compared to usual care, the current evidence remains concentrated primarily on person-centred care integration, with limited studies evaluating broader dimensions of care integration at organisational and systemic levels. These findings highlight the important evidence gaps of DHIs in supporting more comprehensive and system-level integration in cardiovascular care. Further research is necessary to understand the influence of DHI modality and function on effectiveness of care integration.

candidates.title: Low-grade inflammation and cardiovascular events among patients with chronic kidney disease.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Chronic inflammation is associated with cardiovascular disease in the general population, but data on patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are limited. We sought to assess whether systemic low-grade inflammation is independently associated with cardiovascular events in CKD patients not yet on kidney replacement therapy, with or without a history of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD).
METHODS: CKD-REIN is a prospective cohort study of adults with CKD stages 2-5, conducted in 40 French nephrology outpatient facilities. Baseline high-sensitivity plasma C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) was centrally measured using an immunoturbidimetric method. Systemic low-grade inflammation was defined as hs-CRP ≥2 mg/L. Cox proportional hazards models estimated cause-specific hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; composite of stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular death) or hospitalization for heart failure (HHF).
RESULTS: We included 2078 patients: 67% men, mean (SD) age 67(13) years, mean eGFR 36(12) mL/min/1.73 m2, 38% with history of ASCVD, median hs-CRP concentration 2.4 mg/L (inter-quartile range 1.1-5.1). After median follow-up of 5 years, 171 patients had a MACE and 207 had HHF. After controlling for potential confounders, a twofold increase in hs-CRP was associated with a 12% (95% CI 0-26) higher cause-specific hazard of MACE and a 26% (95% CI 13-40) higher cause-specific hazard of HHF.
CONCLUSION: In CKD patients not yet on kidney replacement therapy, systemic low-grade inflammation, measured through hs-CRP, is associated with occurrence of cardiovascular events independently of traditional risk factors, including a history of ASCVD.

candidates.title: Reanimationless Rapid Recovery Versus Thoraco-Abdominal Normothermic Regional Perfusion for Donation After Circulatory Death Heart Transplantation Following Prolonged Asystolic Warm Ischemia.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Donation after circulatory death (DCD) heart transplantation has expanded the donor pool, yet contemporary recovery strategies remain constrained. Rapid Recovery with Extended Ultra-Oxygenated Preservation (REUP) is a non-reanimation DCD recovery strategy that eliminates the need for donor heart reperfusion prior to transplantation. As prolonged asystolic warm ischemic time (AWIT) during circulatory arrest has raised ongoing concerns, whether REUP achieves outcomes comparable to TA-NRP in DCD donors with prolonged AWIT remains unknown.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center study of DCD heart transplant recipients whose donor hearts were recovered using either TA-NRP or REUP and preserved with 10°C static cold storage. Donors with AWIT <10 minutes were excluded. The primary outcomes were severe primary graft dysfunction (PGD) and 90-day mortality.
RESULTS: Eighty-two DCD heart transplant recipients met inclusion criteria, including 55 TA-NRP and 27 REUP recipients. Compared with TA-NRP donors, REUP donors were older (42.0 vs 33.7 years) and experienced longer total ischemic times (285 vs 219 minutes). Severe PGD occurred in 4 TA-NRP recipients (7.3%) and no REUP recipients (0.0%). Ninety-day mortality was 12.7% versus 7.4%, respectively. In weighted bootstrap analyses, REUP was associated with a directional signal toward lower severe PGD (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.09-1.02; directional consistency 97.4%) and lower 90-day mortality (OR 0.56, 95% CI 0.09-2.57; directional consistency 76.3%), although confidence intervals were wide.
CONCLUSIONS: Among DCD heart transplant recipients with AWIT ≥10 minutes, REUP demonstrated early graft function and short-term survival comparable to TA-NRP despite a more challenging donor profile. These findings support further prospective multicenter evaluation of REUP as a broadly deployable non-reanimation DCD heart recovery strategy.

candidates.title: Sedation and anaesthesia in pulsed-field ablation for atrial fibrillation: mechanisms, procedural requirements, and real-world practice.
candidates.abstract: Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) has rapidly emerged as an important energy source for atrial fibrillation ablation, offering tissue selectivity and procedural efficiency while introducing specific anaesthetic and sedation requirements. This narrative review examines the rationale for anaesthesia and sedation during PFA, the mechanisms underlying pain, involuntary movement, and neuromuscular stimulation, and the implications of catheter design, waveform characteristics, and patient-related factors for peri-procedural management. Available evidence indicates that both deep sedation and general anaesthesia can provide safe and effective procedural conditions when supported by appropriate monitoring, airway rescue capability, and experienced multidisciplinary teams. Deep sedation may offer advantages in workflow, recovery, and patient-centred care, particularly for standard pulmonary vein isolation procedures using contemporary biphasic systems with reduced muscle activation, whereas general anaesthesia remains appropriate for complex procedures, patients with substantial comorbidity, or settings in which complete immobility and airway control are essential. Current real-world practice is highly heterogeneous across regions and institutions, reflecting differences in regulations, staffing models, procedural complexity, and local expertise rather than a universally accepted standard. Overall, anaesthetic strategy in PFA should be individualised according to patient risk profile, expected procedural demands, and device-specific stimulation burden. Further prospective comparative studies are needed to define optimal sedation depth, standardise monitoring and outcome measures, and clarify how emerging technologies may enable lighter yet still effective sedation pathways.

candidates.title: The perspective of combining pulsed field ablation and left atrial appendage closure.
candidates.abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) are increasingly discussed as complementary strategies in atrial fibrillation (AF) care, addressing rhythm control and long-term thromboembolic risk. The rationale is attractive, but the current evidence base is uneven. Randomized evidence for LAAC around AF ablation is strongest for thermal-ablation-era workflows, particularly the OPTION trial, which showed lower non-procedure-related major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding with LAAC than with oral anticoagulation (OAC) and non-inferiority for death, stroke, or systemic embolism. Dedicated PFA-specific evidence remains limited to feasibility studies and early observational experience, and no trial has demonstrated that combined ablation-LAAC procedures are clinically superior when the ablation component is performed with PFA rather than radiofrequency or cryoballoon ablation. In parallel, OAC-withdrawal trials after apparently successful ablation, including OCEAN and ALONE-AF, have reported low thromboembolic event rates in selected lower-risk populations, whereas CLOSURE-AF cautions against simple extrapolation of LAAC benefit to older, frailer patients at high stroke and bleeding risk. This review therefore positions combined PFA-LAAC as a potential option for carefully selected patients rather than an established routine strategy. We summarize procedural workflow, patient selection, trial populations, device-platform considerations, reimbursement and organizational issues, and the main uncertainties that should guide future prospective studies.
